lessons.title: Farm assets and types of maintenance
lessons.html:
Why maintenance matters

A farm depends on its physical assets: tractors, planters, sprayers, bakkies, pumps, irrigation systems, boreholes, fences, kraals, handling facilities, sheds, dams and roads. When an asset fails at the wrong moment, such as a planter during the planting window or a borehole pump in a drought, the cost is far more than the repair bill. Lost yield, stressed animals, idle labour and emergency call-out fees all add up. Maintenance management aims to keep assets safe, reliable and economical for their whole working life.

Types of maintenance

TypeDescriptionFarm example
Breakdown (corrective)Repair after failureReplacing a burst irrigation pipe
Preventive (planned)Scheduled work at set intervals of time or useTractor service every set number of engine hours as per the manual
Condition-basedWork triggered by inspection or measurementReplacing worn planter discs found during pre-season check
Daily careOperator checks and cleaningChecking oil, water, tyre pressures and greasing before work

Breakdown maintenance may be acceptable for cheap, non-critical items. For critical assets, preventive and condition-based maintenance are usually cheaper over time.

The asset register

Start with a list of all assets. For each record: description, make and model, serial number, year bought, cost, location, and the person responsible. Mark which assets are critical to production or safety. This register is the foundation of any maintenance plan.

Safety in maintenance

  • Switch off engines, remove keys and lower implements before working on machines.
  • Isolate and lock out electrical supply before working on pumps and motors.
  • Support raised equipment on stands, never only on a jack or hydraulics.
  • Keep PTO and belt guards in place after servicing.
  • Use PPE and keep the workshop tidy, with fire extinguishers available.

lessons.title: Schedules, job cards and records
lessons.html:
Building a maintenance schedule

A maintenance schedule says what must be done, to which asset, how often and by whom. Sources for the schedule include the manufacturer's operator manual, experience on the farm and the seasonal calendar.

  1. For each asset, list the maintenance tasks in the manual with their intervals (hours, kilometres or time).
  2. Add daily operator checks to a simple checklist kept with the machine.
  3. Plan major services and overhauls in the off-season, for example servicing planters in winter and harvesters before harvest.
  4. Include infrastructure: fence patrols, trough and float valve checks, dam wall and spillway inspections, roof and gutter checks before the rainy season.
  5. Display the schedule on a wall planner or in farm software so everyone can see what is due.

Job cards

A job card is issued for each maintenance or repair task. It records:

  • Asset and job number, date and the person doing the work.
  • Description of the fault or service required.
  • Parts and materials used, with quantities and costs.
  • Labour hours and any outside contractor costs.
  • Sign-off when complete and tested.

Maintenance records

Completed job cards are filed against each asset. Over time they build a history showing how often the asset fails, what it costs to maintain and when it may be time to replace it. Record machine hours and fuel use as well; a sudden increase in fuel use can point to a mechanical problem.

Stores and spares

Keep commonly used parts such as filters, belts, shear bolts, fencing wire, drippers and grease in a controlled store. Record stock in and out. Knowing what is on hand avoids long trips to town during critical periods.

Key points

  • Failures at critical times cost far more than the repair itself.
  • Use preventive and condition-based maintenance for critical assets.
  • Keep an asset register as the base of the maintenance plan.
  • Follow manufacturers' intervals and plan major work in the off-season.
  • Use job cards and keep records for every asset.

quiz.question: Which is an example of preventive maintenance?

options.text: Replacing a burst pipe after it fails
Servicing a tractor at the engine-hour interval in the manual
Towing a broken planter to town

quiz.question: What is the foundation of a maintenance plan?
When is the best time to plan a major planter service?

options.text: Never; planters do not need servicing

quiz.question: How should raised equipment be supported during maintenance?
What can a sudden increase in a tractor's fuel use indicate?

options.text: That the diesel price has dropped

PTO guards can be left off after servicing to make the next service easier.
